chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq al-Jariri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever sits between the call to prayer (adhan) of the Maghrib prayer and the call to establish the prayer (iqamah), it is like shedding his blood in the cause of Allah.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And when he intends to say the iqamah, let him recite it until the end of the chapter. Its explanation has already passed with sufficient detail, if Allah wills. And what he mentioned regarding the melodious recitation of the adhan and the rapid recitation of the iqamah, explanation and confirmation of it has also passed in what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for sitting in the mosque between the adhan and iqamah?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the spiritual merit of the interval between the Maghrib Adhan and Iqamah, equating seated devotion during this time to martyrdom. The Sheikh clarifies that the recommended recitation style involves melodious prolongation (tartil) for the Adhan and brisk recitation (hadr) for the Iqamah, a distinction rooted in the prophetic tradition to maintain congregational focus and reverence.
